name: UGC 2773-OT (Hubble)
blurb: UGC 2773-OT, the eruption of a massive star in the dwarf irregular galaxy UGC 2773, seen by Hubble.
label: ugc2773ot-hubble
story: In 2009 a massive star in the dwarf irregular galaxy UGC 2773 flared up in an outburst that looked like a supernova but was not one, sharing traits with the giant eruptions of luminous blue variable stars. Hubble kept watch on the site as part of a survey of recent, nearby supernovae and their impostors.

claims.text: UGC 2773-OT is the 2009 optical transient in the dwarf irregular galaxy UGC 2773, discovered on 2009 Aug. 18.08
It was not a genuine supernova; its progenitor was an LBV and it shares properties with giant LBV eruptions
Program 14149 imaged sites of recent nearby supernovae and SN impostors
'Supernova impostor' as a kind word for this target
